What Waiting (TTFB) measures

Waiting (TTFB) = round trip + server time

  • round trip network latency, there and back
  • server time the server prepares the response

Too many requests to one origin

Requests 1 to 6

  • Each has an open connection
  • Short Queueing

Request 7

  • Six connections already open
  • Long Queueing

HTTP/1.0 and 1.1 only: six connections per origin.

Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 8/8

Save the session as a HAR file

  1. 1Export HAR: the session as JSON
  2. 2Default: no Cookie, Set-Cookie or Authorization
  3. 3Import: drag the HAR file into the table

Open the Network panel, then load the page.

Each request becomes one bar in the Waterfall column.

The Timing tab splits one bar into phases: Queueing, Stalled,

DNS Lookup, Initial connection, Request sent, Waiting, and Content Download.

Waiting, the time to first byte, is one round trip of

latency plus the time the server needs to prepare the response.

Here is an example request with no throttling.

Waiting is the longest bar, and Content Download is short.

Now choose Slow 4G in the Throttling menu and reload.

Waiting and Content Download grow, because both depend on network speed.

On HTTP 1.1, when six connections to one origin are already open,

the seventh request waits, so its Queueing bar grows.

The Initiator column says what started each request.

Priority says how urgent it is.

Hold Shift and hover: initiators turn green, dependencies red.

Export the session as a HAR file, a JSON record.

By default, it leaves out Cookie,

Set-Cookie and Authorization headers, so it is safer to share.
